$x(t)=\,\,$ $2t{e}^{2t}$ $\,\,+{\int }_{0}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,\text{d}s$
{{field-2}} $0$
questions.worked_solution:
Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & t{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At}\,x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & t{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{2(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{2(t-s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{2(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{2(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{s} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t-s} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+{\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t-s} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+g(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $g(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that 

$$
{e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since the initial conditions are given at $t={t}_{0}=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x(0) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{-(t-s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{-(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\text{d}s \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{s=0}^{s=t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
